neet_phy_u20_t06_1.working: Stokes' law gives v_t = 2r^2(ρ-σ)g/(9η), so v_t is proportional to r^2.

neet_phy_u20_t06_3.working: The ball accelerates at first. Placing the upper mark well below the surface lets it reach terminal velocity before timing starts.

neet_phy_u20_t06_4.working: From the formula, v_t ∝ r^2 at fixed ρ, σ and η. So the v vs r^2 graph is a straight line through the origin. R explains A.

neet_phy_u20_t06_5.working: Liquid viscosity decreases with temperature, so the ball falls faster and Statement I is false. At terminal velocity, weight = buoyant force + viscous drag, so Statement II is true.
